## Isotropic viscosity and heat conduction (`forcing/diffusion`) {#sec-ch09-viscosity}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Adds the Newtonian viscous stress, its work, and a Fourier heat flux as face fluxes whose
divergence enters the stage increment.
**Switch.** `forcing/diffusion: {nu_iso, kappa_iso, dynamic, nu_scale_x1, kappa_scale_x1}`; defaults 0, 0,
`false`, none, none. Off unless the key is present and a coefficient is positive.
**Requires.** A `cartesian` grid; $n_{\mathrm{ghost}}\ge2$ for viscosity; an EOS with a positive reference $c_v$
for conduction.
**Order.** Second order in space in the interior; first order in the kernel of the wall normal stress; explicit,
with a parabolic time-step bound.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-viscosity-flux.
:::

The diffusion module is snapy's only closure for sub-grid momentum and heat transport: constant isotropic
coefficients, optionally shaped in $x_1$ (@sec-ch09-x1profile). With the default `dynamic: false`, `nu_iso` is a
kinematic viscosity $\nu$ [m$^2$ s$^{-1}$] multiplied by the face density, and `kappa_iso` a thermal diffusivity
$\kappa$ [m$^2$ s$^{-1}$] multiplied by the face volumetric heat capacity $\rho c_v$. With `dynamic: true` the two
numbers are a dynamic viscosity $\mu$ [Pa s] and a conductivity, still written $\kappa$ but in W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ (NOTATION.md §8), and no density enters.
The heat flux acts on the temperature, not on the potential temperature; so a resting adiabatic column, which is
neutrally stable, is heated in the interior and at the walls (Limits).

The module adds its own time-step bound, $\Delta t\le h_{\min}^2/(2n_{\mathrm{dim}}K)$, which the solver takes
together with the hyperbolic bound before the Courant factor is applied (Chapter 7).

*Aliases.* The removed option `on_theta` (chengcli/snapy#253, #259; removed in #268, which closed #261) is not
part of the code at the pin. Legacy keys `K` and `type` are refused.

### Derivation

All quantities in this layer are per unit volume; $h$ is the cell width, uniform in each direction (the module
refuses every grid but Cartesian). Units: $\mathbf v$ [m s$^{-1}$], $T$ [K], fluxes of momentum [Pa], of energy
[W m$^{-2}$].

#### Continuous fluxes

The Newtonian stress for a fluid with no bulk viscosity is $\boldsymbol\tau = \mu[\nabla\mathbf v + (\nabla\mathbf v)^{\mathsf T} - \tfrac23(\nabla\cdot\mathbf v)\mathsf I]$, and the momentum and energy equations
gain $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol\tau$ and $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\tau\cdot\mathbf v)$ plus the divergence of the
Fourier heat flux, a conductivity times $\nabla T$. Written as fluxes through a face normal to $x_a$, with
$\mu=\nu\rho$ and the conductivity $\kappa\rho c_v$ in the default form,

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{(m_b)}_a &= -\nu\rho\,\big[\partial_av_b + \partial_bv_a - \tfrac23\delta_{ab}\nabla\cdot\mathbf v\big], \\
F^{(E)}_a &= \sum_b v_b\,F^{(m_b)}_a - \kappa\rho c_v\,\partial_aT ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-flux}

and the stage adds $-\Delta t\,\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$ to momentum and energy. With `dynamic: true`, $\nu\rho$ is
replaced by $\mu$ and $\kappa\rho c_v$ by the conductivity $\kappa$.

#### Discrete fluxes

On the face $i-\tfrac12$ normal to $x_1$, between cells $i-1$ and $i$, the code uses

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_1q\big|_{i-1/2} &= \frac{q_i-q_{i-1}}{h_1}, \\
\partial_bq\big|_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12\Big[\frac{q_{i,j+1}-q_{i,j-1}}{2h_b} + \frac{q_{i-1,j+1}-q_{i-1,j-1}}{2h_b}\Big], \\
\overline{q}_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12(q_{i-1}+q_i) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil}

the face-normal difference, the average of the two cell-centred tangential differences, and the two-cell face
average, in `face_normal_derivative`, `centered_derivative` and `face_average`
([`diffusion.cpp:70-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L70-L108)). The divergence $\nabla\cdot\mathbf v$ is formed with centred differences in every cell, `div_vel` ([`diffusion.cpp:467-476`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L467-L476)), and then
face-averaged, `div_face` ([`diffusion.cpp:517`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L517)). The
stress row $b=a$ is $2\partial_av_a - \tfrac23\overline{\nabla\cdot\mathbf v}$, a row $b\ne a$ is
$\partial_av_b + \partial_bv_a$ with the second term dropped when direction $b$ is inactive
([`diffusion.cpp:516-541`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L516-L541)). The viscous work uses the `face_average` of the velocity, and the conductive term
the face-normal temperature difference times the face coefficient of @sec-ch09-wallcoef
([`diffusion.cpp:538-561`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L538-L561)). The tendency subtracts $\Delta t$ times the `divergence` of the three flux arrays
([`diffusion.cpp:566-568`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L566-L568)).

Three properties follow and are checked against a line-by-line port of the module
[check `src/snapy_report/ch09/viscosity_check.py`, output `viscosity_check.out`]:

1. **Conservation.** Momentum and total energy change only by flux differences, so their column sums
   telescope; on a periodic column they are zero to round-off (`[C4]`).
2. **Dissipation.** The kinetic-energy part of the update is removed and the same amount is added to the internal
   energy through the work term; for a random shear the net internal-energy change is positive (`[C5]`).
3. **Accuracy.** For a transverse velocity the tendency is $\nu\rho$ times the three-point Laplacian to round-off,
   which decays a mode of wavelength $\lambda_w$ at
   $4\nu\sin^2\vartheta/h^2 = \nu(2\pi/\lambda_w)^2[1+O(\vartheta^2)]$, with $\vartheta=\pi h/\lambda_w$, second
   order (`[C2]`). The
   normal-stress row acts with the effective coefficient $\tfrac43\nu$, again second order; its stencil is wider
   because the divergence is a centred difference averaged to the face (`[C3]`).

#### Time-step bound

Forward Euler on the $n_{\mathrm{dim}}$-dimensional three-point Laplacian with coefficient $K$ amplifies the
checkerboard mode by $G = 1 - 4n_{\mathrm{dim}}K\Delta t/h^2$, so $|G|\le1$ requires

$$
\Delta t \le \frac{h_{\min}^2}{2n_{\mathrm{dim}}K},
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-dt}

with $K=\max(\nu\varsigma_{\max}^{\nu},\kappa\varsigma_{\max}^{\kappa})$ in the default form ($\varsigma_{\max}$ the largest
value of an $x_1$ profile of @sec-ch09-x1profile, 1 without one) and $K=\max(\mu/\rho_{\min}, \kappa/(\rho c_v)_{\min})$ with `dynamic: true`, in
`max_time_step` ([`diffusion.cpp:572-619`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L572-L619)). At the bound $|G|=1$ exactly (`[C6]`). The solver takes the minimum of @eq-ch09-viscosity-dt and the hyperbolic bound through
`pdiffusion` ([`hydro/hydro.cpp:396-398`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L396-L398)) and then multiplies by the Courant
factor `cfl` (default 0.9; [`meshblock.cpp:528`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L528)), so the diffusive step runs at `cfl` times its limit.

#### What `kappa_iso` diffuses

The energy row receives $\nabla\cdot(\kappa\rho c_v\nabla T)$. At fixed density the internal energy is $\rho c_vT$,
so $\partial_tT = \kappa\nabla^2T$: `kappa_iso` is the thermal diffusivity of $T$. At fixed pressure the heat goes
into enthalpy, $\rho c_p\partial_tT = \kappa\rho c_v\nabla^2T$, and $T$ diffuses at $\kappa/\gamma$ (`[C7]`,
0.714286 for $\gamma=1.4$). A run sits between the two, depending on how fast the pressure adjusts.

On a resting adiabat, $\partial_zT = -g/c_p$ and $\rho\propto T^{c_v/R}$; the flux is uniform in $T$-gradient but
not in $\rho c_v$, and the interior heats at

$$
\partial_tT = \frac{\kappa g^2c_v}{R\,c_p^2\,T},
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat}

$7.93\times10^{-7}$ K s$^{-1}$ per unit $\kappa$ at $T=300$ K for dry air ($R=287$, $c_p=1004.5$ J kg$^{-1}$
K$^{-1}$, $g=9.8$ m s$^{-2}$). The discrete operator reproduces @eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat at second order
(`[C8]`: relative error $1.85\times10^{-6}$, $4.63\times10^{-7}$, $1.16\times10^{-7}$ at $n_1$ = 64, 128, 256).

*Exact and truncated.* Conservation of momentum and total energy is exact. The interior fluxes are second order;
at a reflecting $x_1$ wall the coefficient is second order (@sec-ch09-wallcoef) but the face-averaged divergence in
the normal stress is first order.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-viscosity-stencil shows the stencil of one $x_1$ face in two dimensions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-viscosity-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Stencil of the diffusive flux through the x1 face i-1/2 (orange triangle on the orange face) on a 2-D Cartesian grid. Sky-blue circles are cell-centre primitives. The bluish-green arrow is the face-normal difference across the face; the dashed black arrows are the centred x2 differences in cells i-1 and i whose average gives the cross term of the shear stress. The face coefficient is the two-cell average except at a wall."
#| fig-alt: "Grid of four by three cells with cell centres as circles, one vertical face highlighted with a triangle, a horizontal double arrow across it and two vertical dashed double arrows in the cells on either side."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_viscosity_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Each face flux of @eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil reads the two cells across the face and, for the cross terms and the divergence, their neighbours
in the tangential directions: one ghost layer for conduction, two for viscosity (the face average of a centred
difference reaches two cells), hence the setup check $n_{\mathrm{ghost}}\ge2$. Ghosts are filled by the boundary
functions and the block exchange before the stage (Chapter 11, Chapter 14). Faces at a reflecting $x_1$ wall take
the one-sided coefficient of @sec-ch09-wallcoef; every other face, including seams between blocks, takes the
two-cell average. The module runs in every Runge–Kutta stage, explicit, third in the forcing loop
(@sec-ch09-framework). Evidence for the orders: interior second order from `[C2]`, `[C3]` and `[C8]` (fitted slope
2.00 over three resolutions); the wall coefficient second order from @sec-ch09-wallcoef; the order of the full
operator at a wall through the solver is **not measured**.

1. `DiffusionOptionsImpl::from_yaml` refuses `K` and `type`, checks the keys, and requires finite non-negative
   coefficients and a literal `true`/`false` for `dynamic` ([`diffusion.cpp:246-325`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L246-L325)).
2. `DiffusionImpl::reset` refuses a non-Cartesian grid when a coefficient is positive, viscosity with fewer than two
   ghosts, and conduction without a positive reference $c_v$ ([`diffusion.cpp:334-345`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L334-L345)); it then builds
   the $x_1$ profiles (@sec-ch09-x1profile).
3. `forward` forms the cell divergence `div_vel` ([`diffusion.cpp:467-476`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L467-L476)) and `rho_cv`
   ([`diffusion.cpp:477-481`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L477-L481)), then, per active direction, the face coefficient, the stress rows and
   their work, `momentum_flux` ([`diffusion.cpp:516-542`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L516-L542)), and the heat flux from `dtdn`
   ([`diffusion.cpp:544-562`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L544-L562)).
4. It subtracts $\Delta t$ times the `divergence` of the three flux arrays ([`diffusion.cpp:566-568`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L566-L568)).
5. `max_time_step` returns @eq-ch09-viscosity-dt ([`diffusion.cpp:572-619`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L572-L619)); it throws on a
   non-finite coefficient or a non-positive bound.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Cartesian grids only. `kappa_iso` conducts on $T$, so a resting adiabat drifts. Immersed solids give a wrong face
coefficient by a factor of about 500 (@sec-ch09-wallcoef). No species or tracer diffusion.
:::

1. **Conduction on $T$.** A resting adiabatic column heats in the interior at @eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat, and its
   wall cells cool at the bottom and warm at the top. chengcli/snapy#252 measured the bottom and top cells at
   $-8.60\times10^{-1}$ and $+8.83\times10^{-1}$ K after 1000 steps at $\kappa=75$ m$^2$ s$^{-1}$ and the
   interior within 9 % of @eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat [sha: snapy@69e008452b373b9697c1668eebbd1ea51e7e41e4 on chengcli/snapy main, which is not a pin of this report;
   deck: `tests/test_kappa_adiabatic_rest.py` from a red-test commit recorded in the issue and not in any listed
   repository; run: CPU, recorded in the issue]. The
   remedy `on_theta` was removed in #268; the drift is not addressed at the pin. Re-measuring needs that deck
   committed at the pin: **pending**.
2. **Immersed solids** are read as fluid; see @sec-ch09-wallcoef.
3. **Wall normal stress.** At a reflecting $x_1$ wall the face-averaged divergence takes the cell value, an $O(h)$
   error in the kernel of the normal stress that the wall coefficient does not remove
   (`sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md` §5, "What the fix deliberately does not touch").
4. **Block edges.** Viscosity created $v_2$ beside $x_2$ block edges at an $x_1$ wall row (chengcli/snapy#264),
   fixed by the corner refresh of #265 (Chapter 11). Not re-measured at the pin.
5. **Python setters** on `DiffusionOptions` bypass the YAML checks of step 1 of the walk-through (chengcli/snapy#216).
6. **Time step.** The bound uses the largest coefficient everywhere and the smallest cell width in any direction;
   the one-sided wall coefficient can exceed the cell value by about 17 % at $h/H=0.35$
   (`sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md` §7, off-pin) and is not included. The default `cfl` of 0.9
   covers it; not measured at the pin.
7. **Untested combinations.** Diffusion with an implicit scheme, with sedimentation, or on several ranks is not run
   by any ctest listed here. See the switch coverage matrix (Chapter 12).
